title: Vertex Cover approximation below factor two
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: Do a constant \(\varepsilon \in (0,1)\) and a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm exist which, on every finite simple undirected graph G, output a vertex cover of size at most \((2- \varepsilon )\tau (G)\)?
definitions: Use uniform classical deterministic Turing computation, with no advice or oracle. Integers and rational numerators and denominators are encoded in binary; L denotes the total input bit length. A polynomial bound has constants independent of the input. A vertex cover is a subset S of the vertices containing at least one endpoint of every edge; \(\tau (G)\) is the minimum size of such a set. The graph is represented by its adjacency matrix. The same \(\varepsilon\) and algorithm must work for graphs of all sizes, with no promise on degree, coloring or graph class. An edgeless input requires the empty cover. The question asks for an unconditional algorithm or unconditional refutation of its existence.

context_blocks.text: Vertex Cover is one of the canonical NP-hard covering problems and has a simple factor-two approximation. The absence of a fixed improvement despite extensive work makes the factor a central approximation barrier.

Unique Games implies hardness below two, while unconditional NP-hardness leaves a gap. A restricted graph-class algorithm does not answer the universal target. The source seminar situates the question in the development of approximation algorithms and primal-dual methods.

why: Resolve a basic approximation threshold for a widely used covering primitive.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
